newsitem.title: USA: South Africa's Mbeki says Zaire talks will be soon.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mbeki says Zaire talks will be soon.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Tuesday he was convinced a meeting would take place soon between opposing sides in a bloody conflict in Zaire, but he could not say exactly when.
"Soon" was Mbeki's one-word answer when asked when rebel leader Laurent Kabila and Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko might hold discussions.

"The decision does not rest in my hands," Mbeki told a news conference. "When we saw Kabila in South Africa, he said that he and the Democratic Alliance would like to have discussions as early as possible...In our contacts with President Mobutu, they indicated the same."
Mbeki was in the Washington area to meet with U.S. officials and to attend a summit aimed at attracting capital to Africa.

South Africa, with the collaboration of U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, has hosted several meetings with the two sides in the Zaire war, which led last week to agreement in principle on a Mobutu-Kabila summit in South Africa.
"We are convinced that a meeting will take place," Mbeki said, but noted that the time and place of the talks was not settled.
He also stressed that: "In the event that for whatever reason the meeting does not take place that...the war will continue."

In Kinshasa on Tuesday, Zaire's government vowed its army would never surrender the capital city to advancing rebels and called on residents to be prepared for resistance. Rebels have seized half of Zaire's vast territory since taking up arms in October to topple Mobutu. Kinshasa is the most important city still in government hands.
